summary.headline: Lohia Corp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR503 crore, EBITDA margin 19.9% and order book about INR1,778 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR503 crore versus INR315 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR100 crore (19.9% margin vs 11.5%) and PAT of INR66 crore (13% margin). Management attributed margin expansion to higher volumes, operating leverage and efficiencies, and said it targets about 20% EBITDA margin internally without formal guidance. The order book reached about INR1,778-1,780 crore, up 30% since March 2026 and 195% since June 2025, with about 20% backed by customer advances. Domestic demand now drives the order book, while management expects exports to recover to around 50% of revenue. This was the company's first earnings call after listing.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR17 crore in Q1 FY26; PAT margin 13%

segments.name: Machinery (woven plastic / technical textiles)
segments.commentary: Core business, estimated at 80-85% of revenue. Order book is about INR1,780 crore with about 20% customer advances, and execution quoted at 6-9 months.

segments.name: Spare parts
segments.commentary: Approx. 10-12% of revenue. Management said spare-parts gross margins run 2-3 percentage points above machinery.

segments.name: New initiatives (recycling, monofilament)
segments.commentary: Approx. 5-6% of revenue. Polyolefin recycling only; no polyester recycling yet. Shredding and granulating adjacencies under evaluation.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic approx. 59% and exports approx. 41% of Q1 revenue. Export prices are said to be 10-15% above domestic, net of CIF freight and agency costs.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of 20-25% (no EBITDA guidance given).
Internal EBITDA margin target is about 20%, described as the new normal; management said it will not formally guide on EBITDA.
Capacity is adequate for about INR2,400-2,500 crore turnover. Beyond that, roughly INR80-100 crore capex per INR500 crore of incremental turnover is needed.
Exports are expected to stabilise at around 50% of revenue and order book over time.
R&D spend is expected to average about 3% of revenue going forward.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation stated at about 70-75%; management said peak achievable is about 80-85% across tape extrusion, circular looms and winders.
Maintenance capex and machine balancing continue each year; major capex not yet planned.
Asset turnover of 3-4x; new capacity could go live in 5-6 months, since land is available adjacent to the Kanpur plant.
New products launched: CoEx 1600 multi-layer coating line, Nova 6 Plus six-shuttle circular loom (up to 1,150 picks/min), FIBC cutting and back-cutting machines.
Virtual remote assistance centre set up at Kanpur; TTRC launched a 3-month certification programme for block bottom bag machines.
demand_pricing: Order book is driven mainly by domestic investment; management expects exports to recover to about 50% of revenue and order book.
Conversion of inquiries to executable orders is about 10-15%, over 2-3 years, per management. The current pipeline figure was not disclosed.
Management said Lohia commands 15-20% price premium over Chinese competitors; export competition in Southeast Asia is mainly from Chinese players, and in developed markets mainly from Starlinger.
Margin defence rests on three levers: repricing new orders to current input costs, short- and medium-term supplier contracts, and discount structure tweaks.
Replacement demand is about 3-5% of the order book today and is expected to rise, given 20-25 year machine life.
Management said the tariff does not affect the company directly, as machinery goes mainly to developing countries; customers export fabric to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book rise so steeply from FY24 to about INR1,800 crore, and is this a peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to post-COVID capex recovery, growing non-packaging applications, and single-use plastic bans driving new uses. It said the peak has not yet been reached.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports recover to 40-50% of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export share ranged 45-55% of revenue historically and expects it to stabilise around 50%, though domestic currently leads the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 20% EBITDA margin be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pre-COVID margins were 15-20%, Q1 and Q4 FY26 reached about 20%, and 20% is the new normal internally. It gave no formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is implied for FY27 from the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst suggested INR2,150-2,200 crore; Raj Kumar Lohia said 'should be like that', without confirming the figure.

qa_highlights.question: How much did service and spares contribute, and at what margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares are about 10-12% of revenue, with gross margins 2-3 points above machinery. Consumable parts run about 2-3% of installed plant value each year, perpetually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution cycle for new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 6-9 months, depending on product complexity. Legacy products can be delivered faster and newer, more complex products take longer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D plan and are there hero products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 3% of revenue and expected to stay around 3%. Confidential automation and IoT technologies are in development, but no launch dates were given.

qa_highlights.question: Are any regulations benefiting Lohia against Chinese competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only customs duty on Chinese and European equipment helps. No BIS or other regulatory benefit was identified.

risks_watch: Raw material and component cost volatility; management said it does not hedge purchases through long-term fixed-price contracts with large steel suppliers.
Margin dilution as domestic mix rises during FY27, since export pricing is 10-15% higher; management says margins will be protected.
Chinese competition, particularly in Southeast Asia, where rupee depreciation has been used to offer higher discounts.
Inquiry-to-order conversion of 10-15% and the lack of a disclosed current pipeline figure.
Management did not confirm the FY27 revenue estimate of INR2,150-2,200 crore; watch the Q2 run-rate and order book conversion.
Capacity utilisation figures given in the call were inconsistent (50%, 70-72%, 75%), so the true utilisation level needs confirming.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and margins, with a clear focus on the 20% EBITDA target. Evasive or unprepared on the order pipeline figures, capacity utilisation and export share, which the chairman deferred to later email. The call had audio issues and several figures were corrected mid-call.
key_quotes: For the quarter, we reported revenue from operations of INR503 crores compared with INR315 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, represe nting a growth of around 60%.
So we believe that this is going to be the new normal for us.
So we expect to grow in the range of 20% to 25%.
But we do not give any guidance on the EBITDA number going forward.
We currently are maintaining that we internally target 20% as our EBITDA number.
